name: Women Who Wouldn't Wait
description: Queens, writers, scientists, activists and explorers who pushed past the limits set for women, from Sappho's songs to Malala's school campaign.

checkpoints.name: Ancient voices
checkpoints.note: Hatshepsut and Cleopatra rule Egypt, Sappho writes poems in Greece, Hypatia teaches mathematics in Alexandria, Wu Zetian rules China, and Murasaki Shikibu writes a long Japanese novel.

checkpoints.name: Faith and crown
checkpoints.note: Hildegard of Bingen writes and composes, Eleanor of Aquitaine and Isabella of Castile hold power, Joan of Arc leads an army, Teresa of Ávila reforms her order, and Elizabeth I rules England.

checkpoints.name: Reason and rights
checkpoints.note: Njinga fights Portuguese rule in Angola, Artemisia Gentileschi paints with force, Catherine the Great rules Russia, Mary Wollstonecraft argues in A Vindication for women's rights, and Jane Austen begins writing novels about women's choices.

checkpoints.name: The age of reform
checkpoints.note: Mary Shelley writes Frankenstein, Ada Lovelace imagines computing, Florence Nightingale reforms hospitals, Sojourner Truth and Harriet Tubman fight slavery, Emmeline Pankhurst fights for the vote and Marie Curie wins scientific fame.

checkpoints.name: Modern firsts
checkpoints.note: Virginia Woolf, Frida Kahlo and Simone de Beauvoir reshape art and thought, Amelia Earhart flies the Atlantic alone and Eleanor Roosevelt helps write human rights into world law.

checkpoints.name: Fighting on
checkpoints.note: Rosa Parks refuses to give up her seat, Rosalind Franklin's work helps reveal DNA, and Valentina Tereshkova flies into space. Indira Gandhi and Golda Meir lead nations, while Maya Angelou, Wangari Maathai, Aung San Suu Kyi and Malala carry on.
